y1: Jesus made the boat His pulpit and the shore His auditorium. The slopes by the Sea of Galilee formed a natural amphitheater, so His voice carried far.
y2: A farmer would first scatter the seeds and then plow the field. Because of this, seeds also fell on the path, rocky places, and among thorns. But the harvest of the good soil was 30, 60, and 100 times what was sown. Since a normal harvest back then was 7 to 10 times, this is an astonishing result.
y3: Chapter 13 is the third of the five sermons in the Gospel of Matthew, the 'parables sermon' right in the middle. All seven parables are about 'the kingdom of heaven.' It comes immediately after the rejection intensified in Chapter 12.
y5: The disciples asked, “Why do you speak in parables?” Jesus said, “To you it is given to know the mysteries of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it is not given,” and He quoted Isaiah 6:9–10.
y6: A parable becomes a door to an open heart and a wall to a closed one. Jesus says, “Blessed are your eyes, for they see; and your ears, for they hear.” The disciples were seeing what many prophets had longed to see.
y7: “For whoever has, to him will be given, and he will have abundance; but whoever doesn't have, from him will be taken away even that which he has” (13:12). This isn't about money; it's about hearing. If we respond to the Word we hear, we will understand more; if we neglect it, even what we know will become blurry.
y8: The Path, the Rocky Soil, and the Thorns
y9: The path: When someone hears the Word and doesn't understand it, the evil one comes and snatches it away. The rocky soil: receives it with joy, but since it has no root, it quickly stumbles when trouble or persecution comes.
y10: The thorny soil: hears the Word, but the worries of the world and the deceitfulness of wealth choke the Word, making it unfruitful. These three aren't 'bad people,' but conditions we all have.
y11: The thorny soil is one that outwardly seems to have no problems. There is faith, and they go to church. It's just that so many other things are growing that the Word has no room to breathe. Busyness can be the quietest thorn.
y13: “What was sown on the good soil, this is he who hears the Word and understands it, who most certainly bears fruit and produces, some a hundred times, some sixty, some thirty.”
y14: The good soil has three characteristics: it hears, it understands, and it bears fruit. Even though the amount of fruit differs, they are all good soil. Growth is what matters, not comparison.
y15: The sower generously scatters seed even on the path and the rocky soil. God never gives up on any heart; He sows the Word. Even if there is failure in three places, the harvest from one good soil surpasses all the losses. This parable is both a warning and a hope.
verse: “What was sown on the good soil, this is he who hears the Word and understands it, who most certainly bears fruit and produces, some a hundred times, some sixty, some thirty.”
prayer: God who sows the seeds, I thank You for not giving up on my heart, even when it is like the path, and for sowing Your Word in it. Please clear the stones from my heart and pull out the thorns. Let me be good soil that hears the Word, understands it, and bears fruit. I pray in the name of Jesus Christ. Amen.
d0: parable. It is a story that places the kingdom of heaven next to a familiar scene for comparison. It prompts the listener to think and make a decision for themselves. This is the root of the English word 'parable'.
d1: root. It is the part that grows where it cannot be seen. The root of faith is the time spent alone in prayer and the Word. “Rooted in Christ” (Col. 2:7).
d2: worry. It is the 'worry' we learned about in Chapter 6. Anxiety takes away the space where the Word can grow. Read together with 6:25–34.
d3: understand. It is not just knowing information, but bringing the Word and my life together to understand it. It appears six times in Chapter 13. “Have you understood all these things?” “Yes” (13:51).
